title_original: Australia’s best photos of the month – October 2026
excerpt_original: Dolly Parton, tulips and outback life all feature in the best images captured across the country in October Apartments, community centres and a pink outdoor toilet: Australia’s 2026 National Architecture award winners – in pictures Continue reading...

blocks.text: The dress rehearsal and preview of the Australian Ballet’s The Nutcracker at the Ian Potter State theatre in Melbourne. Photograph: Christopher Hopkins/AAP
An orange rose is seen on the desk of the independent member for Indi Helen Haines during question time in the House of Representatives at Parliament House, 26 October.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP

Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre off the coast of the Madigan Gulf in South Australia. An exceptionally wet monsoon season has brought damaging floods to parts of Australia, but transformed Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre in a way not seen in decades.Photograph: Blake Sharp-Wiggins/The Guardian

The winning Ford Mustang GT of Brodie Kostecki and Todd Hazlewood is wheeled down pit lane to get scrutineered after the 2026 Repco Bathurst 1000 at the Mount Panorama circuit.Photograph: James Forrester/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Cattle are mustered on a property on the outskirts of Quilpie. The opal town, nearly 1,000km west of Brisbane, is looking to expand its tiny population by giving away land and housing grants.Photograph: Lauran Wendleborn/The Guardian

Goalkeeper Javier Lopez of South Melbourne fails to save a goal during the Australia Cup final match between South Melbourne FC and Melbourne Victory FC at AAMI Park.Photograph: Josh Chadwick/Getty Images

Kutcha Edwards, artist and creator of Gugu Dindi Gunyah (Many Rivers, One Home), on stage at the newly renovated Ian Potter State theatre at the Arts Centre Melbourne.Photograph: Charlie Kinross/The Guardian

A couple poses for wedding photos as doctors and members of the Victorian branch of the Australian Medical Association protest outside Parliament House in Melbourne.Photograph: Martin Keep/AFP/Getty Images

Two homeless outreach workers are pictured on the Mornington Peninsula’s Rosebud foreshore. They are concerned about the homeless cohort in the area after a recent spate of deaths.Photograph: Christopher Hopkins/The Guardian

Demolition continues across Lismore, NSW, more than four years after the devastating 2022 floods, with hundreds of flood-affected homes and properties being cleared as part of the government’s buyback and flood recovery programs. Photograph: Elise Derwin/The Guardian
A woman stands next to Erica Zaino’s sculpture ART (Artificial Real Time) at the Sculpture by the Sea outdoor exhibition at Bondi beach. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters
Former dairy farmers Ken and Jill Hooper have spent the past 20 years restoring their property Moona-Bingel, north-west of Deniliquin, NSW. Photograph: Stuart Walmsley/The Guardian
Signage for the Wangaratta law courts. The independent federal MP Helen Haines was critically injured after being struck by a vehicle outside her office on 19 October. Photograph: James Ross/AAP
